notes: Whole-home lighting control systems — scored as SYSTEMS, not individual switches. The unit of scoring is the system platform (e.g., Lutron HomeWorks QSX, Lutron RadioRA 3, Lutron Caseta, Savant Lighting, Control4 Lighting). Lutron dominates: 334 luxury listing sightings. Key differentiators: device/zone capacity, dimming protocol, switch aesthetics, integration depth, and scalability. Ketra tunable lighting is a Lutron-exclusive technology available only through HomeWorks. Performance is NOT flat — tunable white, color temperature range, dimming depth, and scene complexity create real spread.

tier_anchors.notes: HomeWorks QSX: Lutron's flagship panelized system. 10,000+ device capacity, wired QS Link backbone + wireless Clear Connect, exclusive Palladiom/Alisse keypads. With Ketra: adds tunable white 1,400K-10,000K, >90 CRI, one-step MacAdam ellipse Color Lock, circadian automation. The system professional integrators specify for $5M+ homes without hesitation. 334 Lutron sightings in luxury listings dominate the category.

RadioRA 3: Professional-grade wireless, 200 devices/processor, Clear Connect Type X, Sunnata/Maestro/seeTouch keypads. Lutron Designer programming required. Best retrofit solution for $1-5M homes. Savant: Whole-home automation platform with integrated lighting layer. Apple ecosystem integration, TrueImage switch displays, premium app UI. Often paired WITH Lutron hardware for lighting backbone — the fact that professional integrators frequently pair Savant brain + Lutron muscle says something about each system's strength.

Control4: Zigbee mesh, scalable, dealer-channel only. Strong whole-home integration but lighting is one capability within broader automation — not a lighting-first platform. Snap One acquisition (2019) expanded distribution. Caseta: Lutron's entry-level system. 75 device limit, DIY-friendly, Clear Connect RF, no neutral required (most models). Exceptionally reliable but limited scalability and no premium keypad options. The system that introduces homeowners to Lutron before they upgrade to RadioRA 3 or HomeWorks.

Wi-Fi based smart switches. No dedicated lighting protocol — relies on home Wi-Fi network. Individual switch control (not system-level). No scene programming beyond basic app. No professional commissioning. Functional but not a lighting SYSTEM in any meaningful sense. Represents what builder-grade homes install when they want to check the 'smart home' box.
No calibration products. Reserved for products with active safety issues, no UL listing, or documented reliability failures at the electrical level.

quality.notes: THE key differentiator in lighting control — equivalent of cartridge for faucets. Panelized wired (HomeWorks QSX) = centralized dimming modules in panel, clean wall plates, QS Link backbone. Dedicated wireless (RadioRA 3, Caseta) = Lutron Clear Connect proprietary RF, 100x more reliable than WiFi/Zigbee per Lutron's published data. WiFi-based = subject to network congestion, router dependency.

Lutron Clear Connect (Type X for RadioRA3/HomeWorks, Type A for legacy) = purpose-built for lighting with sub-second response and zero interference. Zigbee/Z-Wave = adequate but shared-spectrum. WiFi = congestion-prone, router-dependent.

HomeWorks exclusive: Palladiom (metal, flush), Alisse (hand-finished, 40+ metal finishes). RadioRA 3: Sunnata (touch), Maestro, seeTouch keypads. Savant: TrueImage (customizable display). Control4: Custom Engraved Configurable Keypads. Caseta: Diva, Claro. Leviton: standard Decora.

Custom engraved keypads (HomeWorks, Control4) = multi-button scene control with per-button labels, backlit. Pico remotes (Caseta/RadioRA) = scene capable but limited buttons. Single zone = one dimmer per switch. This is THE aesthetic differentiator that homebuyers notice on the wall.
Lutron: Coopersburg, PA headquarters + global manufacturing (identified). Savant: Hyannis, MA (Apple ecosystem). Control4/Snap One: Charlotte, NC (post-acquisition). Leviton: Melville, NY.

performance.notes: HomeWorks QSX: 10,000+ devices. RadioRA 3: 200/processor (scalable with multiple processors). Control4: enterprise-scalable. Caseta: 75 max. Leviton: per-switch, no system limit but no system management either. Device capacity determines whether the system can handle a whole-home specification.

Ketra: 1,400K-10,000K, 16.7M colors, >90 CRI, Color Lock (one-step MacAdam ellipse), Natural Light circadian. Savant: TrueImage, some tunable options. Control4/Caseta/Leviton: no native color temperature control — dependent on individual bulb capability.
Ketra/HomeWorks: dims to 0.1% flicker-free. RadioRA 3/Caseta: smooth dimming to 1%. Control4: varies by module. WiFi switches: typically 5-10% minimum with visible stepping on some loads.

HomeWorks/RadioRA 3: conditional logic, astronomical timeclock (sunrise/sunset auto-adjust), integration with shading/HVAC/security. Savant: whole-home scenes across subsystems. Control4: strong conditional logic. Caseta: basic scenes via app. WiFi: basic on/off schedules.

HomeWorks + Savant: native integration across AV, HVAC, security, shading — one button press triggers multi-system scenes. RadioRA 3: native Lutron shading + third-party via Lutron Connect. Control4: broadest third-party integration ecosystem. Caseta: HomeKit, Alexa, Google. Leviton: app + voice assistant.

durability.notes: HomeWorks QS Link: wired backbone = physically cannot lose signal. Clear Connect RF: dedicated frequency band, no interference from WiFi/Bluetooth/microwave. Zigbee: mesh improves reliability but shared 2.4GHz spectrum. WiFi: router-dependent, network congestion, firmware update risks.

HomeWorks QSX: dedicated QSX processor, local processing, no cloud dependency. RadioRA 3: dedicated processor, local. Savant: dedicated host (local). Control4: dedicated controller (local). Caseta: Smart Bridge hub (local but single point of failure). WiFi: varies — some cloud-dependent.
Lutron systems: typically 8-year warranty on components. Savant: 3-year standard, extended available. Control4: 2-year standard. Leviton: 5-year.

HomeWorks/RadioRA 3: requires Lutron-certified installer with Lutron Designer access. Savant: authorized dealer only. Control4: authorized dealer only. Caseta: DIY-friendly. Factory certification ensures system is properly commissioned — field performance of professional vs DIY installations is markedly different.

Lutron: direct manufacturer support + nationwide dealer network (largest in category). Savant: dealer network. Control4/Snap One: dealer network + Snap One distribution. Leviton: retail replacement (Home Depot, Amazon).

Lutron: Founded 1961, HomeWorks lineage since 1990s, Clear Connect since 2009. Proven 20+ year field performance on wired systems. Savant: Founded 2005, 18+ years. Control4: Founded 2003, 22+ years. Leviton: Decora Smart is newer product line within 100+ year company.

scoring_rules: Score the SYSTEM PLATFORM, not individual switches or dimmers. Lutron HomeWorks QSX is one scored product. A single Caseta dimmer is part of the Caseta system product.
Lutron platform hierarchy: HomeWorks QSX > RadioRA 3 > Caseta. These are legitimately different products with different architectures, not badge-engineering. Score separately per Rule 19.

Ketra is a Lutron-exclusive technology available ONLY through HomeWorks. HomeWorks with Ketra and HomeWorks without Ketra are different scored products per Rule 19 (different capabilities at component level).
Savant as lighting-only vs Savant as whole-home: Score the lighting control capability specifically. Savant's AV/climate integration is a report finding, not a lighting score finding.

Professional integrators frequently pair Savant brain + Lutron lighting hardware. This is a MATERIAL FINDING — it means the market itself views Lutron as the superior lighting-specific hardware. Report this.
Control4/Snap One acquisition (2019): Snap One acquired Control4. Now part of broader Snap One dealer ecosystem. Report corporate structure.

DIY vs professional installation: Systems requiring professional commissioning (HomeWorks, RadioRA 3, Savant, Control4) score differently than DIY (Caseta, Leviton) on certification spec. This is a quality/reliability signal, not snobbery.
WiFi-based systems (Leviton, generic smart switches) are fundamentally different architecture than dedicated lighting protocols. WiFi switches are individual devices, not a system. Score accordingly.
Lutron 334 luxury listing sightings — dominant category presence. Report this market data.
Corporate structure = report finding. Lutron Electronics Co. is privately held (Coopersburg, PA). Snap One (Control4) is publicly traded. Savant Systems is privately held.
